sense: for tennis, basketball and other ball games

terms.comment: The ball court of a Roman villa: Pliny’s in Tuscany plūra genera exercitātiōnis plūrēsque circulōs capit, room for several games at once (Ep. 5.6.27).
Andresian’s word for the court; the lexicon, with Traupman (p. 53), uses it for the playground (see playground).

phrases.latin: In sphaeristēriō lūditur pilā, quam alter mittit, alter excipit, et remittit rēticulō.
phrases.english: In the ball court they play with a ball, which one throws and the other catches and sends back with a racket.

sources: Lewis & Short: sphaeristerium · Lewis & Short: aula · Lewis & Short: lusorius
